subject.title: [Bug] Agent automatically executes config commands from example code without user confirmation

question: Should OpenClaw add a hard confirmation boundary for model-initiated OpenClaw self-management shell commands now, or wait for the broader response-level tool confirmation design?
rationale: Current source proves the gap, but the fix changes the authorization contract for trusted full/off exec, provider configuration, model defaults, gateway lifecycle commands, and channel-visible approval UX.

options.title: Design the boundary now
options.body: Add a maintainer-led policy that always confirms or denies model-initiated OpenClaw config/model/gateway lifecycle shell commands while documenting compatibility and escape hatches.

options.title: Fold into the canonical gate
options.body: Keep this issue as evidence and implement it as part of the broader response-level confirmation gate tracked in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/23451.

options.title: Keep full/off unchanged
options.body: Document that trusted full/off exec intentionally permits these commands and rely on operator policy configuration instead of a new hard boundary.

recommendation.title: Design the boundary now
recommendation.body: Add a maintainer-led policy that always confirms or denies model-initiated OpenClaw config/model/gateway lifecycle shell commands while documenting compatibility and escape hatches.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans security defaults, config compatibility, and the extracted agent-core execution loop where recent ownership history is strongest.
